Birth Right

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Unregistered Midwives deliver 4 dead babies in 18 months

Further information:
Bingala works as a designer for a tailor in Muizenburg. One day a woman named Caitlyn Collins comes into the store, they get chatting and Bingala tells her that his wife Ennie is 4 months pregnant and how they don’t really want to deliver in a state facility. Collins says she is a midwife and offers to facilitate a home delivery for the couple as a kind of trade exchange, Bingala would do some clothing for her. Bingala’s mom in Malawi is a midwife so he has a lot of respect for the profession and agrees.

Caitlyn then comes to see Ennie 6 times at the couple’s home, according to the couple she hardly ever checks the heartbeat, but she does do measurements and a basic examination of the pregnancy. Ennie goes for one scan at 11 weeks and after that Caitlyn insists that the couple don’t need a back OB or scans, she says that the body knows what it is doing, and she is healthy, so her baby is healthy. Ennie says she is sure she can hear two heart beats, but Caitlyn says that she is way to small to be carrying twins

At 10 months pregnant Ennie has passed the mark where a midwife should legally continue without getting the patient to consult an OB or induce. For a single pregnancy this has now become a risky delivery, but again Caitlyn explains that it is fine and their one baby is doing well.

Ennie goes into labour, they call and call, but only 6 hours later does Caitlyn show up.
She turns down the lights and tells everyone to remain calm, she then proceeds to fall asleep on the couple’s bed. Bingala keeps waking her to update her on the delivery.
12 hours after Ennie’s labor began Caitlyn finally notices that there were two babies and that one is breached and the other one is still in the sack that is halfway out. She panics and tells the couple she is not equipped to handle this kind of delivery that they needed to go to the emergency. She agrees to drive them but instructs them not to tell anyone that they were trying for a home delivery, they must say that labor just started.

Long story short, the delivery took way too long and due to the bad management of the midwife, Ennie and Bingala’s twins pass away in the womb due to asphyxiation.

They came to us, and we investigate Caitlyn. It turns out she is not a registered midwife in South Africa, so legally she is not allowed to deliver babies at home or in a hospital setting. She did her midwifery training through the North American Registry of Midwives and is part of a collection of radical ‘midwives’ who believe that the birthing process needs to be unmedicated and the power given back to the women. On social media she talks a lot about how a woman’s body know how to birth her child that there should be no interference in this natural process, woman just need to access their wild woman to birth successfully.

Together with another unregistered midwife, Ruth Ehrhard, she formed the ‘Circle of Elephants’ and as a team they have been doing home births in Cape town CBD, Cape Flats, Simons Town, and cape peninsula area. But after 3 stillbirths in 18 months, late 2019, 2020 and early 2021, the circle of elephants disbanded.

ERNIE
I just wanted my child to be born, like, in my own home whereby she could feel more welcomed.

25-year-old Ernie Chirwa and her husband Chifundo Bingala where expecting their first baby in February this year and they wanted a home delivery with a midwife.

CHIFUNDO
my mother is a midwife.
Midwife is work of bringing babies to earth They are respected people.

While they were searching for the right midwife the couple were introduced to this woman, Caitlyn Collins. The couple were told that she is a renowned midwife within the Cape Town home birthing community and would offer them a peaceful and safe home delivery.

CAITLYN COLLINS INSTAGRAM
Video – Hey Mumma

At 4 months pregnant Ernie starting seeing Collins for her monthly prenatal check-ups

MASA AND CHIFUNDO AND ERNIE
On those six or so occasions that she came to check up on you. What was she doing?
She could just come with a stethoscope and check on my baby's heartbeat and she could praise my tummy just to feel it.
But she used to struggle to get the heartbeat.

According to experts, as their midwife, Collins should have been checking Ernie’s blood pressure, doing regular urine tests and she should have advised the couple to do a 26 week scan, which according to them she never did.

ERNIE
she told me that she would do all the necessary things which are supposed to be done during the process. as being the first mum I didn't know what were this things supposed to be done


Ernie and Chifundo believed that Collins was a legitimate Midwife and so they trusted her.
39 weeks became 40 and then 43. Ernie was concerned, but she says Collins reassured that her baby would be fine.

ERNIE
She said it's normal for the first time, Mother, to be over. That's what she said.

According to Angela Wakeford who has been a private midwife for over 29 years, this was not within midwifery protocols and a dangerous decision for collins to have made






ANGELA WAKEFORD
That was a very overdue long pregnancy. Usually. you prefer if the lady goes from gets to 42 weeks at the latest you should be referring in?
M: And what are those dangers of leaving a woman pregnant to 43 weeks?
The danger is that the increased risk of stillbirth.

Ernie went into labour on the 13th of February At 6pm and around 8pm they called Collins, who promised to arrive soon. but she only showed up at midnight at which point Ernie was in excruciating pain

ERNIE:
she switched off the lights and then just slept. Then around 2 a.m., that's when my sac came out. I told my husband, Can you check on me, please? Something is coming out of me.
That's when he came to her and woke up.
So she switched on a torch and checked on me and she was like, This is the sack That means the baby's coming at any minute.. And then time kept on going.
so she slipped again.

Angela Wakeford
M: Ernie says. When her set came out, Caitlin then went and slipped. Now, what should have actually happened?
Well, she's obviously in very active labor at that stage. So really should have she should have been
Monitoring of labour midwives checking on her, listening to Heartbeat, doing a vaginal examination to assess whether she's still in first stage of labour or ready to pursue. And that would have then she would have then found that the baby was in a breach position.

At around 5 the next morning Chifundo woke Collins again to say enough is enough and something needs to be done to help his wife.

ERNIE:
That's when she realized that the baby food was coming out and she was like, You know what, guys? This is what is called place labor. I've never done and I've never delivered such a situation. I can't handle this.

As a breech baby with her feet coming out first, Ernie and Chifundo’s daughter was in danger of asphyxiation due to a cord prolapse, which is when the umbilical cord is constricted during labour, cutting off the babies oxygen supply

Then she was like, We need to wait, maybe do a full eat. That's when my husband said, no, there's no way we have to wait. This is too much. We need to take it to the hospital.
And at this point, you've got baby's foot coming out of you.

Collins then drove Ernie and Chifundo to retreat a state midwife Obstetric unit. She dropped them at the front door, told them not to mention her name or that they were doing a home birth

ANGELA WAKEFORD
M: At that point, what should have Caitlin done?
Transferred her straight to Mowbray Maternity to the referral hospital,
and instead
she took her to a midwife obstetric unit.
Whould she have known that that wasn’t the correct place to take Ernie

At retreat they confirmed that the babies cord had prolapsed and while they waited for an ambulance to transfer Ernie to Mowbray maternity hospital, the largest dedicated maternity hospital in south Africa, the nurses confirmed that babies heart beat had stopped

my babies stopped breathing. I realized that I wouldn't have my baby anymore.

Only once their babies were dead, were Chifundo and Ernie informed that they were expecting twins.
Their daughter had died during labour, and their son at least 24 hours earlier

ERNIE
The died before the labour started. So he gave up his life to his sister.

Ernie and Chifundo had lost their twins, which at this point they believed was an unavoidable process of labour. That was until they were informed that these were not the first babies to die in Collins care. Two other babies had died in 2020 and 2021.


LINK ABOUT SANC

In 2011 Collins received a certificate as a certified professional midwife through the North American Registry of Midwives, but she never registered with the South African Nursing Council, making her practice illegal.
Collins speaks candidly about operating outside of the law in this Podcast interview done with the free birthing society

Collins podcast
The South African Nursing Council seems to have a say over who call themselves a midwife and who doesn't in South Africa. So they basically own that word, which is just insane.

According to her numerous social media posts as a midwife Collins fundamentally believes in the sovereignty of birth and that woman can birth instinctively, without any medical intervention

Collins podcast
when I started my own practice, it's like I intuitively I didn't do these things like vaginal exams


In 2015 Collins and a colleague started a home birthing practice called circle of elephants . After two babies died under their care the private midwives in Cape town, including Angela Wakeford, called a meeting and it was here that Collins explained what happened with the first baby that passed in 2020

ANGELA:
All I know is that.
She had ruptured membranes for a week. The water is released, the water is broken.

When a woman’s waters break the amniotic fluid that is vital to keeping the foetus safe is released and labour will normally take place within 24 hours, but with every passing day the risk of infection getting into the uterus and infecting the baby drastically increases

ANGELA:
If this was a mom to be that you were looking after, how would you have prevented that?
I would have been afraid and hostile to 24 hours. That's protocol.

The second baby that passed in 2021 was primarily under the care of Collin’s colleague, according to our source the babies foetal heart rate dropped and then due to a lack of communication the mom was transferred in too late, and the baby passed

ANGELA:
Why weren’t they stopped?
We didn’t have the authority to stop them and I they weren’t registered with SANC so I don’t think there was anything that they could do

When we contacted the South African nursing council for an interview IT declined, and even though IT IS the regulatory body for midwives in South Africa, IT stated that it was unable to investigate unregistered midwives

It was the doctors at Mowbray Maternity hospital that filed an official complaint about Collins and the circle of elephants to the western cape department of health in 2021. After this complaint that department issued them a warning to stop practising and register with the south nursing council

I'm really actually quite amazed that I managed to navigate. That kind of playing the game but not playing the game for as long as I did it ended up in in a year ago kind of getting like being investigated by the Department of Health

In early 2021 the doctors at Mowbray Maternity hospital, filed an official complaint about Collins and the circle of elephants to the department of health. It was after this complaint that department issued them a warning to stop practising and register with the south nursing council

COLLINS PODCAST
So what? How did the investigation whole thing go?
So it was pretty much around the fact that we don't carry drugs and that's dangerous.
and it was also something along the lines that they said, because you allow women to do what they want to do at birth, you're a threat to their safety.
That was the crux of it.
And so we have we did stop our practice And we stopped in July this year

In November 2021 issued Collins posted this video on her Instagram, again expressing her contempt for the law and the modern medical world

CAITLYN COLLINS INSTAGRAM VIDEO

Collins never stopped, in certain circles she started calling herself a birth keeper, which she says is someone that holds space for woman labouring at home, but offers no medical intervention. But to Ernie and Chifundo they trsuted her as their midwife

CHIFUNDO
This would be always our fault. Because our babies talk to us through trials.
Because our trusting in someone who is in the field for many, many years and she's experienced that person in that sector.

Their babies were dead and the woman they had trusted to deliver them safely was nowhere to be seen. A few after the death Chifundo confronted Collins about abandoning them at the hospital

Ch: you acted like you gave us a lift. You just wanted to drop us then you go on your way.
M: but I'm not allowed to the hospital.
Ch; You are not allowed in the hospital, why?
M: none of the midwives I who work in cpt can go into the hospitals.
Ch: You couldn’t even speak to them, I was having this patient..I’m a midwife
M: No…because
Ch: Because you are not around
M: no, this is part of in the whole world. At the moment, that the medical, the western medical hospitals don’t want midwives, they don’t want to talk to midwives, they aren’t willing to work with midwives.
M: again, want to say I'm sorry..but the way that I was in the moment, trying I think, MY ABSOLUTE BEST, to support you and it wasn’t good enough for you.
I tried my best..

Mowbray Maternity hospital declined to speak to us, but Wakeford shared this report detailing its findings into the Ernie and CHifunso’s twins deaths
It is evident in this case that Ms Collins lacked the training and skill necessary to identify and safely manage the risk factors that made this pregnancy high risk. Additionally, it is unacceptable that she never examined Mrs Chirwa in labour.

In your experience, Angela, for Caitlin to have had three deaths in just a space of 18 months, is that high?
It is a high statistic.
What would be on average?
Well in the registered midwife homebirth community in Cape Town over the last 20 years there have been two baby deaths and both of those times it was unavoidable.
That puts it into perspective.
00:54:49:15 - 00:54:50:07
Yes, I do.

After numerous attempts to reach Collins we went with Chifuno to try and get some answers from her directly

CONFRONT TRANSCRIPT

Yes, Caitlyn. It’s me, Chifundo, here.
I want to talk to you.
Would you mind to come outside here?

[Caitlyn] I’m not going to come outside.

After Collins refused to come out her husband arrived

[Masa] We’d like to speak to Caitlyn Collins.
[Collin’s Husband] Ja, she has said that she can’t talk to you.

[Masa] We just want to know: is she still birthing babies? And we want to know what happened in Chifundo and Ernie’s case.
[Collin’s Husband] Chifundo and Ernie do know exactly what happened.

[Masa] No, we would like to know. We’re doing an investigation.
[Husband] I’m not going to comment.

[Masa] Four babies have died under Caitlyn’s care!

[Husband] Okay, please… please…

[Masa] I’m talking to you. I’m saying to you your wife is continuing with birthing babies…

[Husband] Please don’t film this.

[Masa] …even though she’s been told by the Department of Health to stop.

[Husband] I’m not engaging with you.

[Husband] I’m sorry for what’s happened to you. And I’m sorry that you’re dealing with this.

[Chifundo] No, you’re not sorry!
[Masa] Now you’re sorry that he’s lost his twins - after being negligent? After telling them that they’re not carrying twins?

Hey, Caitlyn! Caitlyn!

Collins never came down to answer to us or Chifundo, which was extremely painful for Him

The family have subsequently opened a case with the South African Police services

The western cape department of health have also put a multi-disciplinary team together to investigate Collin’s Practices

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Unregistered Midwives deliver 4 dead babies in 18 months
metadata.Further information: Bingala works as a designer for a tailor in Muizenburg. One day a woman named Caitlyn Collins comes into the store, they get chatting and Bingala tells her that his wife Ennie is 4 months pregnant and how they don’t really want to deliver in a state facility. Collins says she is a midwife and offers to facilitate a home delivery for the couple as a kind of trade exchange, Bingala would do some clothing for her. Bingala’s mom in Malawi is a midwife so he has a lot of respect for the profession and agrees. Caitlyn then comes to see Ennie 6 times at the couple’s home, according to the couple she hardly ever checks the heartbeat, but she does do measurements and a basic examination of the pregnancy. Ennie goes for one scan at 11 weeks and after that Caitlyn insists that the couple don’t need a back OB or scans, she says that the body knows what it is doing, and she is healthy, so her baby is healthy. Ennie says she is sure she can hear two heart beats, but Caitlyn says that she is way to small to be carrying twins At 10 months pregnant Ennie has passed the mark where a midwife should legally continue without getting the patient to consult an OB or induce. For a single pregnancy this has now become a risky delivery, but again Caitlyn explains that it is fine and their one baby is doing well. Ennie goes into labour, they call and call, but only 6 hours later does Caitlyn show up. She turns down the lights and tells everyone to remain calm, she then proceeds to fall asleep on the couple’s bed. Bingala keeps waking her to update her on the delivery. 12 hours after Ennie’s labor began Caitlyn finally notices that there were two babies and that one is breached and the other one is still in the sack that is halfway out. She panics and tells the couple she is not equipped to handle this kind of delivery that they needed to go to the emergency. She agrees to drive them but instructs them not to tell anyone that they were trying for a home delivery, they must say that labor just started. Long story short, the delivery took way too long and due to the bad management of the midwife, Ennie and Bingala’s twins pass away in the womb due to asphyxiation. They came to us, and we investigate Caitlyn. It turns out she is not a registered midwife in South Africa, so legally she is not allowed to deliver babies at home or in a hospital setting. She did her midwifery training through the North American Registry of Midwives and is part of a collection of radical ‘midwives’ who believe that the birthing process needs to be unmedicated and the power given back to the women. On social media she talks a lot about how a woman’s body know how to birth her child that there should be no interference in this natural process, woman just need to access their wild woman to birth successfully. Together with another unregistered midwife, Ruth Ehrhard, she formed the ‘Circle of Elephants’ and as a team they have been doing home births in Cape town CBD, Cape Flats, Simons Town, and cape peninsula area. But after 3 stillbirths in 18 months, late 2019, 2020 and early 2021, the circle of elephants disbanded.
